definitions.explanation: A small round French confection made of two almond-meringue shells sandwiching a cream or jam filling. Sold in bright pastel colors and treated in Japan as a stylish gift sweet.

examples.japanese: マカロンを{三|みっ}つ{買|か}った。
{色|いろ}とりどりのマカロンが{箱|はこ}に{並|なら}んでいる。
examples.english: Colorful macarons are lined up in the box.

examples.japanese: {手土産|てみやげ}にマカロンを{持|も}っていったら、{子|こ}どもたちがとても{喜|よろこ}んだ。
examples.english: When I took macarons as a gift, the children were delighted.

notes:
Counted with 〜{個|こ}. Popular as a small gift or souvenir because the colors photograph well and the boxes are attractive.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- マカロンを{食|た}べる: to eat a macaron
- {色|いろ}とりどりのマカロン: colorful macarons
- マカロンの{詰|つ}め{合|あ}わせ: an assortment of macarons
- マカロンカラー: pastel "macaron colors"

SIMILAR WORDS:
- マカロニ: macaroni — a completely different word despite the similar sound
- メレンゲ: meringue — the whipped egg white the shells are made from
- {焼|や}き{菓子|がし}: baked sweets — the shop category macarons are usually sold under
